key_insight: A mean-flow adjoint framework built on homogenized lattice Boltzmann methods enables sensitivity analysis for unsteady porous-cylinder flows without the prohibitive checkpointing costs of fully transient adjoints.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical route to gradient-based design and control of porous bluff-body systems across laminar, unsteady, and turbulent regimes.
method: Model cylinders as local porous media with Brinkman penalization in HLBM
Use mean-flow adjoint sensitivity analysis for drag and energy-dissipation objectives
Generate LES adjoint kernels automatically via differentiation, including SGS turbulence terms
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a systematic study from steady laminar to unsteady and turbulent flow, including a proof-of-concept at Re = 3900 that compares automatic-differentiation-based adjoints with the frozen turbulence assumption.
watch_item: Mean-flow and frozen-turbulence approximations may limit gradient fidelity in strongly chaotic flows, so implementation and validation against full transient sensitivities remain important.
paper_title: Mean-Flow Adjoint Sensitivity Analysis of Unsteady Flow Around Porous Cylinders Using a Homogenized Lattice Boltzmann Method
